p: thee from the womb: He treated and chose you from the beginning of his own mercy, and before you could merit anything.
whom I have chosen: Whom God accepts as righteous: or who had opportunity to it because of the law, and your holy calling.
thirsty: Because man of himself is as the dry and barren land, he promises to moisten him with the waters of his Holy Spirit, Joel 2:28, Joh 7:38, Ac 2:17.
shall spring up as among the: That is, your children and posterity will increase wonderfully after their deliverance from Babylon.
shall call himself by the name: By this diversity of speech he means one thing, that is, that the people will be holy, and receive the true religion from God, as in Ps 87:5.
I am the first: I am always like myself, that is, merciful toward my Church, and most able to maintain it, as in Isa 41:4,48:12, Re 1:17,22:13.
call: And appoint them that will deliver the Church.
it in order for me: That is, tell me how I should proceed in this.
ancient people: God calls the Israelites ancient, because he preferred them to all others in his eternal election.
them show to them: Meaning, their idols.
ye are even my witnesses: Read Isa 43:10.
their delectable things shall not profit: Whatever they bestow on their idols, to make them seem glorious.
they see not: That is, the idolaters seeing that their idols are blind, are witnesses of their own blindness, and feeling that they are not able to help them, must confess that they have no power.
god: Meaning that whatever is made by the hand of man, if it is valued as a god, is most detestable.

profitable for nothing: By which appears their blasphemy, who call images the books of the laity, seeing that they are not only here called unprofitable, but in Isa 41:24 abominable. Jeremiah calls them the work of errors, Jer 10:15, Habakkuk, a lying teacher Hab 2:18.
fellows shall be ashamed: That is, who in any way consent either to the making or worshipping.
stand up: Signifying, that the multitude will not then save the idolaters, when God will take vengeance, although they excuse themselves by it among men.
hungry: He describes the raging affection of the idolaters, who forget their own necessities to set forth their devotion toward their idols.
the house: To place it in some Temple.

warm himself: He sets forth the obstinacy and malice of the idolaters who though they see by daily experience that their idols are no better than the rest of the matter of which they are made, yet they refuse the one part, and make a god of the other, as the papists make their cake god, and the rest of their idols.
eateth flesh: That is, he either makes a table or trenchers.

for he hath shut their eyes: The prophet gives here an answer to all them who wonder how it is possible that any would be so blind as to commit such abomination, saying that God has blinded their eyes, and hardened their hearts.
on ashes: He is abused as one that would eat ashes, thinking to satisfy his hunger.

Remember these: Showing that man's heart is most inclined to idolatry, and therefore he warns his people by these examples, that they should not cleave to any but to the living God, when they should be among the idolaters.
Sing: He shows that the work of the Lord toward his people will be so great, that the insensible creatures will be moved with it.
tokens of the liars: He arms them against the soothsayers of Babylon, who would have said that they knew by the stars that God would not deliver Israel, and that Babylon would stand.
servant: Of Isaiah and the rest of his prophets, who assured the Church of God's favour and deliverance.
deep: He shows that God's work would be no less notable in this their deliverance, than when he brought them out of Egypt, through the sea.
Cyrus: To assure them of their deliverance he names the person by whom it would be, more than a hundred years before he was born.
